description: The configuration surface of the kubernetes chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

controlPlane.description: The control plane, which runs as pods in the management cluster.

replicas.description: How many copies of the API server, controller manager and scheduler to run. Two survives a node failure; one is offered for development. ⚠ Unlike an etcd quorum this is a plain replica count — the datastore is separate and is shared — so an even number is not the mistake it would be on a Raft member set.

controlPlaneCpu.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Platform-chosen. A Kubernetes API server's working set is a function of the objects in it rather than of anything on this form, so a "control plane size" would be a number nobody can choose correctly. It is also what the quota meters reserve against.

dataStoreName.description: The Kamaji DataStore the control plane keeps its state in.
dataStoreName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: A DataStore is CLUSTER-SCOPED, so it cannot be a per-tenant object this platform creates — it is installed with Kamaji and named here. ADR-009 asks for a dedicated etcd per tenant and this is not that; see conformance.yaml § owed.

enabled.description: Whether the control plane's own metrics endpoints are scraped. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ It covers the control plane, which runs in the management cluster. Nothing scrapes inside the cluster being created; that needs an agent in the bundle.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

network.description: The address space of the cluster being created.

podCidr.description: The CIDR block pods are addressed from. ⚠ It must not overlap the management cluster's own pod or service range, and nothing checks that — an overlap produces a cluster whose nodes route the platform's addresses to themselves.

serviceCidr.description: The CIDR block Service cluster IPs are allocated from. The same overlap warning applies.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

serviceDomain.description: The DNS domain of the cluster being created.
serviceDomain.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Cluster API does not default it and Kamaji freezes it on first write, so it must be set at creation and can never be changed. Every chart and sidecar in the ecosystem assumes cluster.local, so it is a constant rather than a setting.

version.description: The Kubernetes minor version of the control plane. The patch level is the platform's. ⚠ Upgrade the control plane before the node pools and by at most one minor at a time; a node pool may run up to three minors behind and may never run ahead. Neither rule is enforced by this API today — an illegal pair is refused by the cluster's own admission, after the create was accepted.
